subject: tool:gdl-memory-graph
value: A QUERY THAT RUNS DURING A BUILD HAS NO STATISTICS, AND PROFILING THE BUILT ARTEFACT WILL NEVER SHOW YOU WHY IT IS SLOW. memory_graph's `_import_exact_name_candidates` joins binary_symbol to itself on normalized_name and ran for 8.61s of a 15.09s `build_database` -- 57% of the whole graph build, and 73.8% once it was made set-based and paid the join twice. The join is not slow: the IDENTICAL query answers in 0.00s against the finished database, over the same 21,206 rows, producing the same 1,373 pairs. The difference is WHEN it runs. `ANALYZE` executes at the END of build_database, so mid-build SQLite has no statistics for the tables it just populated and fell back to `binary_symbol_raw_name_idx (platform, symbol_kind, raw_name)` for the INNER table -- an index that constrains nothing in this query -- turning an indexed lookup into a scan of all 7,405 Xbox functions for each of 2,989 GameCube ones. 22 million row comparisons, 8.79s for the COUNT and 8.61s again for the INSERT. `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` run against the finished DB shows the CORRECT plan and confirms nothing; it must be run against the mid-build connection to see the defect at all. THE FIX IS ONE CLAUSE: `JOIN binary_symbol x INDEXED BY binary_symbol_name_idx`, which makes the plan independent of whether statistics happen to exist yet. Measured after: 8.61s -> 0.01s, full build 15.09s -> 6.45s. GENERAL FORM: any query inside a population step -- an importer, a migration, a census that queries the rows it is writing -- is planned without statistics, so its index must be PINNED rather than inferred, and a profile taken against the finished artefact is measuring a different query plan than the one that runs.
